newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND, ITALY AGREE ON CLOSER TIES, NATO GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: POLAND, ITALY AGREE ON CLOSER TIES, NATO GROWTH.

text.p: Poland and Italy agreed to boost economic and cultural ties on Monday as the visiting Italian prime minister confirmed his country's support for Warsaw's bids to join NATO and the European Union.
"We support Poland's efforts aimed at membership in NATO and the EU," Romano Prodi said after meeting his Polish counterpart Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz.
Poland hopes to be among the first former Soviet bloc countries that are due to be invited to join NATO at the pact's Madrid summit in July, despite strong opposition from Russia.
It expects to begin talks on EU entry in early 1998.

Both prime ministers said relations between the two countries, military foes before the collapse of communism in 1989, were excellent but further strengthening of economic and cultural links was desirable.
Cimoszewicz said Poland and Italy would sign an agreement on strengthening cultural links during a coming visit by Rome's culture minister.
The Polish government would organise a seminar in Italy on privatisation of Poland's companies to attract more Italian investors, he said.
"We have welcomed big Italian investors but we feel there are not enough small and medium-size ones," he said.
Italy's Fiat Spa , which has invested nearly $900 million to manufacture cars in Poland, is the country's biggest foreign investor.
Cimoszewicz also said he agreed with Prodi that the two countries' economic experts would meet in May to discuss ways of reducing Poland's large deficit in trade with Italy.
Italy, Poland's second biggest trading partner after Germany, had a $1.6 billion trade surplus on exports of $2.6 billion in the first three quarters of 1996.
Prodi, on a two-day official visit, was scheduled to meet President Aleksander Kwasniewski and other top state officials later on Monday. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
